subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Do maintainers accept removing `sanitizeInboundSystemTags` outside the queued-event path after confirming that every remaining external-text path reaching a model prompt is protected by a structural envelope or another mechanical boundary?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes a prompt-injection defense boundary across core, channel plugins, SDK inputs, stored transcripts, and native clients; source-level intent alone cannot decide the desired trust contract.

options.title: Confirm structural isolation
options.body: Review the complete prompt-bound external-text inventory and merge only after each route is proven envelope-isolated or otherwise mechanically unable to impersonate trusted prompt structure.

options.title: Retain broader neutralization
options.body: Keep a narrowly defined sanitizer at remaining external-text ingress points if any prompt route lacks a structural isolation boundary.

options.title: Split the refactor
options.body: Land non-security label and SDK cleanup separately, then propose the sanitizer-contract change with a focused security review.

recommendation.title: Confirm structural isolation
recommendation.body: Review the complete prompt-bound external-text inventory and merge only after each route is proven envelope-isolated or otherwise mechanically unable to impersonate trusted prompt structure.

likelyOwner.reason: The related merged prompt-context work and current product boundary make this the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate available.
